claims.text: The material family is AlCoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloys.
These alloys are multiphase under the relevant aging conditions.
Aging between 600 and 1000 °C produces a ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
The initial equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi ingot is a chemically homogeneous, single-phase BCC supersaturated solid solution without long-range chemical order.
Relevant processing consists of aging for 15 hours at 600 °C or 1000 °C under argon followed by water quenching.
Mechanical testing is performed at ambient temperature after aging.
Intermediate-temperature aging near 600 °C forms L2_1-ordered superlattices.
The L2_1 ordering occurs specifically in Al-rich regions.
L2_1 ordering induces lattice distortion and hardening.
At higher aging temperature, the ordered structure undergoes phase decomposition or disordering.
A nearest-neighbor BCC lattice-gas model can predict order-disorder transitions in high-entropy alloys.
Ordering at 600 °C increases yield strength and reduces ductility to a brittle state.
At 1000 °C, thermal energy overcomes the ordering enthalpy.
Disordering or phase decomposition at 1000 °C relieves lattice strain and restores ductility.
The sample aged at 600 °C has significantly lower uniform tensile ductility than the as-melted sample.
The sample aged at 1000 °C recovers ductility to a level comparable to or above that of the as-melted sample.
The as-melted alloy has high ductility because it lacks long-range chemical order and has a homogeneous BCC structure.
L2_1 ordering is thermodynamically favorable over an approximately 600–800 °C critical range.
The alloy remains ductile above 1000 °C and below 400 °C.
The lattice-gas model omits lattice-distortion and lattice-vibration effects, limiting the accuracy of its ordering predictions.

contradictions.description: The intervention uses aging at exactly 600 °C and 1000 °C, whereas the conditions require temperatures strictly between 600 °C and 1000 °C.

The initial material is described as as-melted, while the baseline calls the same state 'as-melted (solutionized)'; solutionizing is a separate heat treatment and is not included in the stated processing.
